scope: Mathematical derivations and deterministic implementation checks

proof_notes.energy: A sum of nonnegative squares is zero iff each v_k-u_k <= 0.
proof_notes.reflexivity: Every coordinate satisfies u_k >= u_k, so E(u,u)=0.
proof_notes.antisymmetry: u>=v and v>=u imply equality in every coordinate.
proof_notes.transitivity: u>=v and v>=w imply u>=w coordinatewise.
proof_notes.triangle_bound: relu(w-u) <= relu(v-u)+relu(w-v) coordinatewise; monotonicity and the triangle inequality of the Euclidean norm give sqrt(E(u,w)) <= sqrt(E(u,v))+sqrt(E(v,w)).
proof_notes.scc_quotient: Mutual reachability is an equivalence relation. A cycle between distinct quotient components would make those components mutually reachable, contradicting their separation.

threshold_counterexample.conclusion: The positive-threshold relation is not transitive.

randomized_triangle_check.note: Random checks test implementation; the proof is above.

discrete_graph.semantics: Reflexive graph reachability; input edge truth is assumed.

held_out_edge_demo.evaluation_type: Logical closure of supplied edges over seen node IDs

limitations: No empirical SNLI or other natural-language accuracy is measured here.
Theorems concern the exact vector order and graph relation, not a learned encoder's semantic correctness.
Graph closure can propagate incorrect learned edges; a path witness proves only derivability from supplied edges.
An unseen edge among known nodes is not zero-shot generalization to unseen sentences.
Sentence entailment is a preorder; quotienting by semantic equivalence yields a partial order.
Graph SCC equivalence need not be real semantic equivalence when edges are noisy.
Order energy alone distinguishes entailment from non-entailment, not contradiction from neutral.
Natural-language inference does not by itself identify intervention effects.

primary_sources.title: Order-Embeddings of Images and Language (ICLR 2016)
primary_sources.relevance: Reversed product order, order-violation energy, and binary SNLI adaptation.
